Hi all, and welcome to Prompt of the Day. For those of you tuning in -- check us out. We post pictures, people write. The subverse has been pretty dead, so I asked around and found out why there's so little content. And the answer is just pretty much all across the board:

We're in an emotional situation where we feel so drained and blank that we can't seem to focus nor write to save our lives. I hope today we are able to explore that a little bit and maybe create some content.

The Challenge:

This week we will be writing about being helpless. The point it to express and pin point how exactly we are feeling at our lowest, and explore ways to elaborate upon them to make others understand (and consequentially ourselves)

The Prompt

You may write as yourself or through a character.

The story begins in the middle of things. You awaken in a unfamiliar place. Slowly you look around and try to piece together your surroundings; however, it's hard to see. Squinting, you see a figure standing not too far away. You cannot see the figure's face. The figure explains that you are at a crossroads. Fearful, you look around for anyway out. The figure shakes it's head. You realize you can't go back. Puzzled, You ask the figure why you are here.

The figure walks closer, just barely concealed.

"You tell me."

Guidelines

-Specific prompt, do with it what you will.

-Address your fears, address the issues.

-Why are you there?

-Make it as long or as short as you want, just convey your message.

-Plot twist!

Happy...eh... well... good writings,

A CHALLENGER APPROACHES - Challenge Prompt, Emotional Writer's Block Edition!

In the summertime air, Martin Astronaut languished. The heat danced across his skin. His eyes slowly set themselves to open and congealed around a dimly lit central vision, a ceiling fan spinning at some distance, beating out an odd meter. So he turned his head, and a cat crossed the doorway. These images, though, remained unfamiliar.

“I know things,” he thought, “In particular I know the things in my house. I know what was here when I fell asleep. I have no fan. I have no cat, no doorway.”

These odd images soon became troubling. He sat up quickly, stubbing his toe against some unseen object in the darkness. Words of pain leapt from his lips. Given to want, he reached to his breast pocket and found a familiar object, a pack of cigarettes, and lazily drew one to his mouth. The flame from his lighter pirouetted across the cigarettes tip, illuminating other facets of the room.

As the cigarette came to life, somewhere in the corner an odd silhouette lingered.

“Hey Marty,” said the silhouette, cravingly pivoting from the corner.

“Hey, what brings you here?” said Martin bemused.

Came the response: “You…tell…me…”

It was long and drawn out in a fearful slur, pursued by wicked movements that led the silhouette into the dim light, and then did its attributes become more intricately defined.

Certainly, Martin Astronaut recognized it as himself. Not in his exact form, though. The silhouette contained splotches of flesh cobbled together, strings of burnt hair, a smile stripped of lips, and dotted with teeth. The panic began to quell.

“That’s pretty well close,” said Martin, clumsily drawing on the cigarette.

Still the figure advanced.

The fear was now palpatable in his voice, “This place, explain it!”

Came the response: “You…tell…me…”

Now, other silhouettes emerged from the corners of gloom, hands of mangled bone grasping at his side, Martin dropping to the ground, pinned beneath the foul odor, howls leaping from his belly.

The burning that came was nothing like the summertime air. Drops of liquid splashed across his tingling flesh, the mangled vision of himself now grasped the flame that once pirouetted across his cigarette, and placed it to his skin. Beset from all sides, Martin Astronaut died.
